rules.rule: Check for urgent leg symptom conditions
rules.problem: Type and trigger right; every red-box item is present. Only gap (omission, not distortion): the DVT 'especially if' risk factors (BMI > 30, smoker, immobile, pregnant, oestrogen, leg trauma, recent hospitalisation, TB, cancer) are not checked for; the page treats them as likelihood modifiers, not required criteria, so this is acceptable.

rules.rule: Check leg symptoms not needing urgent attention
rules.problem: Type and trigger right. The six joint-screen findings come from the page's top screening line, which precedes the red box and applies to every leg-symptom patient, not specifically to the 'not needing urgent attention' approach; the task name is slightly misleading but the role (check_for consumed by the joint-problem rule) is right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable fracture of leg (leg symptoms)
Diagnose probable acute limb ischaemia (leg symptoms)
rules.problem: and/or structure matches 'Sudden severe leg pain at rest with any of ... numbness, weakness, pallor, no pulse'. Only the pallor concept choice (c039) is open.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable critical limb ischaemia (leg symptoms)
rules.problem: and/or structure matches 'Muscle pain ... on exercise associated with pain at rest, ulcer or gangrene'.
OR of six findings matches 'If joint warm/tender/swollen or unable to do all actions comfortably, joint problem likely'. 'Arthropathy' is a fair SNOMED reading of 'joint problem' (page sends to 77).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable sciatic nerve irritation (leg symptoms)
rules.problem: Branch gate (no leg swelling) plus buttock pain radiating down the leg matches the page; 'Sciatica' for 'Irritation of sciatic nerve' is right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable peripheral vascular disease (leg symptoms)
rules.problem: Intermittent claudication is also the first condition of the urgent critical-limb-ischaemia rule, so a patient with claudication plus rest pain/ulcer/gangrene gets both PVD probable and CLI probable. The page puts PVD under 'not needing urgent attention'; clinically CLI is a form of PVD and the priority rule still fires, so the effect is a redundant diagnosis rather than a missed urgency. Optional: add (no …) of the three CLI-associated findings.

'Recent' is dropped from 'Has there been a recent injury?' (c066), and 'Joint swelling' carries no leg site (c065). Also, because the rule uses the same unqualified Injury of lower limb as the fracture rule, an injured patient who cannot bear weight gets sprain probable alongside fracture probable even though the page reaches sprain/strain only in the 'not needing urgent attention' approach; consider (no Unable to weight-bear). Sprain and strain are split into two identical-evidence rules so both diagnoses always fire together; the page offers one undifferentiated 'Sprain/strain likely'.
Identical evidence to the sprain rule; same dropped 'recent' (c069), same site-less Joint swelling (c068), same co-firing with the urgent fracture rule.

rules.rule: Urgent: leg symptoms with fracture, DVT or limb ischaemia
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention ... Refer urgently.' Structure (and <presenting complaint> (or active_condition ×4)) follows the house pattern; all four red-box diagnoses are present.

summary: Nothing is invented: all 76 conditions trace to the page in the right rule and role, and all 41 SNOMED concepts exist. The most consequential issues are in the sprain/strain pair: the page's 'recent injury' is encoded as any Injury of lower limb (a (snomed_concept "Recent" "qualifier value") exists), 'Swelling over one joint' has no leg site, and the two rules share identical evidence with the urgent fracture rule's injury finding so they co-fire with fracture and with each other. Lesser points: 'pallor' as White discoloration of skin where Pale complexion is SNOMED's pallor concept, and the PVD rule overlaps with critical limb ischaemia via the shared Intermittent claudication finding.
